community interests. And may some of you remember this is a resolution that we were directed to take 
a look at, and to look at some metrics to determine really what parcels floated to the highest and best 
use for particular purposes.  
[3:19:32 PM] 
And some of the things that we were to take a look at is distance from high frequency and real transit 
stops. Our opportunity mapping metrics, job proximity index, job activity corridor, park deficiencies, 
certainly assigned public elementary schools and other city priorities. Inclusive of lot sizes, floodplain, 
distance to nearby amenities. I'm happy to say that we are very close to releasing our report to the 
Austin city council. We believe that we have several different tracts that may not have come up in 
conversations along the way that really doing a drill down analysis with the office of real estate services

taking a look at housing implications related to our policies. And the fair housing assessment now -- it 
used to be called the fair housing impediment study, is actually that.  
[3:21:34 PM]

segments that involve aid, it involves often times Travis county, the city, and it's really taking a look at

consultant, because that's what we would typically want, is we would want a consultant to come in and I

interesting perspective to get that third-party brokered look at whether there's impediments or not.

Austin and aid have a potential to partner, but it isn't necessarily something that would fall squarely on 
the plate of the city. So because we are a participating jurisdiction and that means we get hud funding

jurisdictions to be more collaborative with other agencies within their community that can impact fair

embrace you in that work. We anticipate bringing in interlocal agreement to council in the next coming 
few months and what that will require is going out and working with the other entities to ensure that 
the boards, for example, the commissioners' court, is interested in partnering with that work.
